quarterly_data.signal: Q3 FY2026 results: CEO George Kurian reported Q3 revenue of $1.71 billion, an increase of 4% year-over-year (up 6% excluding the divested Spot business), with operating income and EPS at record highs; CFO Wissam Jabre said non-GAAP EPS was $2.12, up 11%, exceeding the high end of guidance, and non-GAAP gross margin was 71.2%.
quarterly_data.figure: Q3 revenue $1.71 billion, up 4% year-over-year (6% ex-Spot); EPS $2.12, up 11%; gross margin 71.2%

quarterly_data.signal: All-flash: 'another record all-flash array revenue quarter, growing 11% year-over-year to $1 billion in Q3 for an annualized run rate of $4.2 billion', as data center customers use all-flash arrays to meet density and power requirements.
quarterly_data.figure: all-flash array revenue $1 billion in Q3, up 11% year-over-year; annualized run rate $4.2 billion

quarterly_data.signal: AI demand: in Q3 approximately 300 customers selected NetApp to prepare their data for AI and as the storage foundation for AI; Kurian said a year ago it was 'around 100-plus wins, it's now close to 300'. Within the quarter's AI mix, roughly 60% were still in data prep / data readiness / data lake models and 40% were in production training or production inferencing use cases; momentum across public sector, manufacturing, health care and life sciences, financial services and early adoption in semiconductors.
quarterly_data.figure: approximately 300 customers (AI) in Q3 vs around 100-plus wins a year ago; roughly 60% data prep, 40% production

quarterly_data.signal: AI product ramp: AFX, NetApp's disaggregated storage system purpose-built for AI, had strong early momentum in its first quarter of shipment with significant wins in neocloud, financial services and semiconductor, including a model training and fine-tuning win at a neocloud and 'a win in a large Asian neocloud this quarter'. Kurian said AFX was ahead of expectations but, as a new architecture requiring customer qualification, NetApp is 'not predicting a ramp like you saw, for example, with the C-Series'. The AI Data Engine (AIDE) early access program was highly successful and AIDE 'will be generally available in Q4'.

Memory-price inflation hit product margin: Kurian described 'unprecedented inflation in memory prices'; NetApp raised prices at the start of the quarter (roughly in line with the market, more on AFAs than HFAs) and will do so again as needed, typically giving customers 90 days to 120 days to adjust purchasing. Jabre said product gross margin declined by 4.2 percentage points sequentially to 55.3%, primarily on unfavorable revenue mix and, to a lesser extent, market purchases to meet unexpectedly higher demand for certain products; the long-term product gross margin target remains mid-50s to high 50%. Hard-drive price increases are 'nothing compared to' NAND.
quarterly_data.figure: product gross margin 55.3%, down 4.2 percentage points sequentially

quarterly_data.signal: Supply: Kurian said 'We are not experiencing any supply shortages at this time and are not aware of any that is upcoming', while anticipating 'pricing and the sort of the tight supply environment to continue for a period of time'. NetApp qualifies multiple suppliers per component and is working to bring alternate silicon into specific configurations with longer lead times (it uses off-the-shelf merchant silicon with multiple qualified suppliers); lead times are not uniformly extending. On HDDs, NetApp does not buy the highest capacity HDDs, 'which are the ones that are more constrained', and feels good about procurement. Jabre said fiscal 2026 is still mostly covered from prebuys made earlier in the year, with some open-market replenishment in Q3 and possibly Q4.

Media-mix response to NAND inflation: after the price increases, customers are having more discussions about hybrid flash arrays (HFA), Keystone and cloud alternatives; Kurian said it is 'too early' to call it a trend but 'HFAs are starting to see a lot of interest from customers', and NetApp's broad portfolio (unlike all-flash-only competitors) lets it serve price-sensitive workloads.

Guidance (non-GAAP): Q4 revenue of $1.87 billion, plus or minus $75 million, implying 8% growth at the midpoint (9% excluding Spot), gross margin 69.5% to 70.5%, operating margin 30.5% to 31.5%, EPS $2.21 to $2.31. Fiscal 2026 revenue now $6.772 billion to $6.922 billion (midpoint $6.847 billion, 4% growth), EPS $7.92 to $8.02. Kurian said Q3 results were not a result of pull-ins and the Q4 guide does not rely on pull-ins; large deals worked on for many quarters partly closed in Q3 and more are expected to close in Q4.
quarterly_data.figure: Q4 revenue $1.87 billion, plus or minus $75 million (8% growth at midpoint); FY2026 revenue $6.772 billion to $6.922 billion ($6.847 billion midpoint)

quarterly_data.signal: Backlog: deferred revenue was $4.63 billion, up 12% year-over-year; remaining performance obligations were $5.11 billion, growing 14%; unbilled RPO, 'a key indicator of future Keystone revenue', was $482 million, up 38%. Keystone storage-as-a-service revenue grew approximately 65% year-over-year.
quarterly_data.figure: deferred revenue $4.63 billion (+12%); RPO $5.11 billion (+14%); unbilled RPO $482 million (+38%); Keystone revenue up approximately 65%

quarterly_data.signal: Public cloud: Public Cloud revenue of $174 million was flat year-over-year and up 17% excluding Spot, driven by first-party and marketplace services, which grew 27%; about half of revenue from new first-party and marketplace customers came from new-to-NetApp customers. Public Cloud gross margin was 85.1%, at the high end of the 80% to 85% long-term range. Growth levers include connecting into 'the AI growth rates of the hyperscalers'.
quarterly_data.figure: Public Cloud revenue $174 million (up 17% ex-Spot); first-party and marketplace services up 27%; Public Cloud gross margin 85.1%
